messages:
elaine: FYI urgent — customer acme-prod is getting routed to us-east even though x-region: eu-west. Seeing 500s/400s, auth failures, and big latency. Ticket TKT-14287 opened. Can someone take a look?

sam: omg ok tagging eng-oncall. do we have any traces or request ids? is this just a subset of requests or all traffic?

elaine: attaching headers from one failed request:
```
:method: POST
:authority: api.redwood.example
:path: /v1/generate
host: api.redwood.example
x-region: eu-west
authorization: Bearer <redacted>
user-agent: acme/1.2.3
```
response: 401 from us-east cluster, trace id x-trace-id=trace-0a1b2c

pranav: quick hypothesis: Envoy L7 steer is supposed to match x-region -> route to eu-west cluster, but kernel/route config might have been partially rolled out. Could be a header normalization/ttl or header-ttl rewrite on the edge.

liam: deploy-bot shows a gw-config rollout yesterday at 03:12 UTC (v2.14.0 -> v2.15.1). pinging deploy-bot for details. :warning:

deploy-bot: [automated] rollout gw-config v2.15.1 started at 2026-03-17T03:12:08Z, canary groups: 10% -> 25% -> 100%.

maria: I queried the gateway admin routes on a canary node. header match rule missing for header named 'x-region' on route table 4 for cluster us-east-1. cmd: `curl http://gw-canary-3:9901/config_dump | jq '.configs[] | select(.name=="routes")'` -- shows match has `:authority` and `x-region-legacy` but not `x-region`.

sam: that would explain it. any quick repro we can share with support/customer? eli, can you run a curl hitting the edge vip with explicit header?

elaine: repro here (from our support runbook):
```bash
curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.example" -H "x-region: eu-west" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://edge.vip.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Response: routed to cluster=us-east-1, 401, body: {"error":"issuer_mismatch"} trace: trace-0a1b2c

pranav: action plan: 1) stop rollout / roll back gw-config to v2.14.0 2) set temporary header rewriting rule on edge to preserve x-region -> x-region-header 3) capture full L7 logs and traces for failing requests 4) postmortem later.

liam: I can trigger the rollback if we have approval. sam, liaise with infra-sre for the rollback window.

sam: approving emergency rollback under incident rules. I’ll open an incident and set severity P1. 

ops-bot: [incident] Incident INC-2026-089 opened by sam: "gw-config canary missing x-region match => cross-region misroute". Paging oncall.

maria: quick debug note — I enabled verbose route logging on canary nodes:
```
[2026-03-17T03:18:45Z] envoy router: matched virtual_host "api.vhost" route "generate-v2" - header_matches: [:authority, x-region-legacy] -> cluster "us-east-1"
[2026-03-17T03:18:46Z] request id=trace-0a1b2c: rewrote headers: set x-region -> (removed)
```

elaine: customer impact: auth failures (401) because us-east issuer doesn't accept eu tokens; retries triggered extra requests and we saw ~25% token usage spike. support ticket has screenshots of 500s on the client side.

liam: rolling back now. running: `deployctl rollback gw-config --to v2.14.0 --force --reason "emergency route mismatch"`

deploy-bot: [automated] rollback initiated for gw-config to v2.14.0 by liam at 2026-03-17T03:22:10Z.

ops-bot: enabling temporary header-preserve hook on edge to map x-region -> x-region-legacy for all incoming requests.

pranav: also creating a query to search logs for any other header name mismatches: `grep -R "x-region-" /var/log/envoy/* | wc -l` and scanning config diffs for route_match changes.

sam: noted — also check whether this caused any billing anomalies for acme-prod customer. finance might need a credit if we see extra tokens billed.

elaine: updating ticket TKT-14287 with repro steps + traces. sharing dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/gw-routing?orgId=1 (link for internal use).

deploy-bot: [automated] rollback completed successfully at 2026-03-17T03:38:19Z on 100% of nodes.

liam: monitoring. initial checks show new requests now route to eu-west as expected. canary logs show header_matches include x-region again.

ops-bot: emergency fix: header_preserve hook applied and gw-config reverted. Marking incident as mitigated pending postmortem.

elaine: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open until postmortem. would like a follow-up on: why the x-region key name changed in the rollout, and why the canary checks didn't catch it.

pranav: will own the postmortem and config diff. next steps: collect config diffs, test harness to validate header match rules, and add an automated canary check that simulates header-based routing for each region.

eli: (customer reply) "Thanks for the quick action. We're seeing normal traffic now but please keep us posted on credits for the extra usage."

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-089 status -> mitigated at 2165437099.
